review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–130) and judged it against the repeated-proof-machinery rubric only. I did not open the imported files or search other sources, because nothing in this file needed it. Almost every declaration is a one-line term that applies an existing lemma and restates its type with `type_of%`. Examples are `postShuffle_native_values`, which just applies `postShuffle_barFree_values`, and the `nativePure*`, `totalFree*` and `summandFree*` chains. The only tactic proof is `valueOfComposite`, a single `rw [← ModuleCat.comp_apply, equality]`. That is a short routine unfolding, so it does not meet the rubric's bar for nontrivial repeated reasoning. The `hg` and `hh` hypotheses in `postShuffle_native_values` are written twice, once for A and once for B. That duplicates statement text, not proof reasoning, and the proof of this theorem is a single application. The `nativePureLeft` and `nativePureProof` steps differ only in which factor (A or B) they feed to `nativeComposite_tensor`, and each is a thin wrapper. I found no block of nontrivial mathematical reasoning repeated across two proofs. The main uncertainty is whether the other proofs in the library, which I did not inspect, repeat the same arguments. That is outside the scope of this file.
